# R4 parameter-environment matrix — loop 1/3

This is a finite grammar/effect equivalence-class enumeration: 8 parameter forms × 11 body-declaration forms × named/callback × sloppy/strict/module, plus initializer effects, callable-kind exceptions and early errors. Each semantic cell has JS, TS and TSX captures. Arbitrary initializer calls and effects are not bounded by this matrix; the discovered design boundary is explicit. This is not an exhaustive correctness certificate for arbitrary ECMAScript expressions.

Normative derivation: [ES2025 FunctionDeclarationInstantiation](https://tc39.es/ecma262/2025/multipage/ordinary-and-exotic-objects-behaviours.html#sec-functiondeclarationinstantiation), [IteratorBindingInitialization](https://tc39.es/ecma262/2025/multipage/syntax-directed-operations.html#sec-runtime-semantics-iteratorbindinginitialization), [ContainsExpression / parameter early errors](https://tc39.es/ecma262/2025/multipage/ecmascript-language-functions-and-classes.html#sec-function-definitions-static-semantics-early-errors), and [Annex B block functions](https://tc39.es/ecma262/2025/multipage/additional-ecmascript-features-for-web-browsers.html#sec-block-level-function-declarations-web-legacy-compatibility-semantics).

Simple parameters share the variable environment; parameter expressions create the body environment and its same-name var copy, except names supplied by hoisted body functions. Initializers select their undefined-argument arm in parameter order; reads/writes to uninitialised self/later formals throw. Closures retain the environment where they are created. Only sloppy simple parameters receive mapped arguments. Arrows capture arguments, this and new.target. Body lexical collisions and non-simple-parameter use-strict directives are early errors. Non-simple patterns without expressions do not cause the body split.

Ground truth is the synthetic Node output in node-matrix.jsonl (actual values and errors, not exit codes). P means parameter binding; B means the distinct body var binding. Binding descriptions derive from these rules, with closure-separated controls distinguishing equal-valued bindings. main/head full rows and labels for EVERY language are in matrix-cell-records.jsonl; the compact tables below reproduce endpoints, owners and labels. JSON contains all owner spans, access/path/line/end-byte fields.

OK/FIXED-here are seam classifications, with per-cell executable assertions in classify_matrix.py; inherited line-CFG/alias precision is not recertified. OUT-OF-MODEL parity failures are unresolved failures of the requested fail-closed policy, not accepted exceptions. DESIGN-CHANGE cells are STOP. Source-bound Rust RED/GREEN tests supplement these fixture assertions.

Classification counts: {"OK": 264, "OUT-OF-MODEL": 373, "FIXED-here": 120, "DESIGN-CHANGE": 6}

Regression outcomes: {"PASS": 384, "EXCLUDED": 379}

# R7 grammar-derived extension

Pinned inventory: grammar-inventory-preaudit.json (node-types.json hashes), actual whole-file parser facts kind-parser-facts.jsonl. Runtime required/optional wrappers use pattern; name-field alternatives come from tuple_parameter aliases, not runtime formal lists (vendored common/define-grammar.js:672–690,746–762). readonly is unnamed; named modifier nodes are accessibility_modifier and override_modifier; decorators have their own field. JS formal children expand pattern plus assignment_pattern. TS/TSX formal children are required_parameter/optional_parameter and pattern expands nine alternatives.

| Formal kind or field | JS | TS/TSX | Positive non-simple evidence | BoundNames / audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|identifier|direct|wrapped|no|decoded binding|
|undefined|direct|wrapped|no|binding recognized; PR-A ordinary-list Def support remains conservative|
|assignment_pattern|direct|value field in wrapper|yes|left binding only; default RHS ignored by invalid-target proof|
|object_pattern / array_pattern|direct|pattern field|yes|binding children only; keys and types excluded|
|rest_pattern|direct|pattern field|yes|binding child; supported identifier rest Def rules retained|
|member_expression / subscript_expression|pattern supertype|pattern field|no|positive invalid BindingElement proof; refusal independent of simplicity|
|non_null_expression|absent|pattern field|no|positive invalid BindingElement proof|
|required_parameter / optional_parameter|absent|formal children|value or wrapped non-simple pattern only|no-value identifier/undefined/this is simple after erasure|
|this|absent|pattern field|no|erased; no runtime BoundName|
|accessibility_modifier / override_modifier|absent|wrapper children|no|public/private/protected/override do not make a default|
|readonly (unnamed token)|absent|wrapper token|no|not a default|
|decorator|absent|wrapper decorator field|no|no inferred default from the decorator's presence|
|type_annotation and tuple name aliases|absent|erased type context|no|type traversal fenced; tuple names are not callable formals|
|unrecognized kind|not grammar-listed|not grammar-listed|never|unit negative control; no broad unknown-kind non-simple inversion|

200 language cells:40 JS,80 TS,80 TSX = supported kind × strict/sloppy × named/callback. Each cell compiles original JS or a recorded TS erasure with Node; malformed binding targets compile original annotation-free source because TS transpilation repairs malformed syntax and would be inadmissible. TS erasure proves ES behavior, not TS type correctness; modifier/decorator carriers exercise grammar fields, with valid TS surface placement limited to constructor parameter properties/decorators.
